title: Givers and takers
header_line: Jose's analysis of a book we are still naming. Not a summary of the book. Not affiliated with or endorsed by the author or publisher.

lines.text: Who pays when the bill comes, and who waits?
A student said a determined person is committed to completing one task. Jose said: where in their life have they shown a long-term goal that they achieved? That is a big one for me.

He told of a man he swam with in high school whose only goal since he was a little boy was a gold medal in one event. That is a person whose entire life was the discipline of getting to that race, he said.
A student said: the ability to overcome, and being proactive. You can wait until everybody starts a task to do yours, or you can be proactive.
Are you a long-term or short-term thinker? Jose asked. Some people tell you what you want to hear, but they really want to take care of themselves right now. That is a bad sign.

Another sign: you are about to do business with somebody, and when the bill comes they don't even look at it. They wait for you to pick up the bill, every time. A student said: people who want to pay will fight you for the check.

Givers and takers, he said. It's not about how much money you have. Sometimes people with a lot of money are even worse. Do you ask your partner: what can I do for you to improve? What can I do for the company?
You should have fifty or sixty things that screen people, Jose said. Also think about your messaging: are you ready for the sacrifice, the pain, the threshold of risk?
A student said it has become a popular trend. Jose said: so many people tell us they are entrepreneurs, and a month later: no, I just need a salary.
A student said: if you are a co-founder, help me build it. If I have to pay you full price, why am I giving you equity? Jose said: that is the long-term thinking.
Somebody who spends three hours talking about the mission, Jose said, versus somebody who asks: how much are you paying? A student said: how well do they perform under pressure, and for how long?
Give me proof, he said: you can make it, and you have the habits and the makeup. They are not going to learn this on the job.
What proof would you ask for, and what proof can you give?

exercise.title: Five minutes
steps: Write a long-term goal you have achieved and how long it took.
Write who on your team is a giver and who is a taker.
Write how you would test a person under pressure.
Write the sign you look for when the bill comes.
Write what proof you can give that you can make it.

check.q: What did Jose ask about a person's life?
choices: Where have they shown a long-term goal they achieved?

check.q: What did Jose say about the bill?
choices: Notice whether they look at it or wait for you to pay every time

check.q: What did Jose say you should be asked for?
choices: Proof that you can make it

recap: Look for long-term goals achieved. Notice givers and takers. Ask for proof, and give it.
